c-291.summary: Xylitol, safe for people, is very dangerous to dogs and even small amounts can cause low blood sugar and liver damage. Keep sugar-free gum, candy and some peanut butters out of a dog's reach.
c-291.principle: A dog's pancreas mistakes xylitol for glucose and releases insulin sharply, so blood sugar plunges. The risk of xylitol ($\mathrm{C_5H_{12}O_5}$) is gauged by dose per weight $D=\frac{m}{m_{\mathrm{body}}}$.
c-291.example: A 10 kg dog can drop in blood sugar from only about 0.1 g/kg (about 1 g) of xylitol, and above about 0.5 g/kg (about 5 g) liver damage becomes likely. One piece of sugar-free gum typically holds about 0.2-1 g, so a few pieces reach the danger range.
c-291.actionItem: Today, move sugar-free gum and candy out of bags, pockets and drawers to where your dog cannot reach. If a dog ate some, bring the ingredient label and call a vet right away.

c-292.title: Why Alkaline Hot Spring Water Feels Slippery
c-292.summary: The slippery feel of alkaline hot springs comes from skin oils turning soap-like. If your skin is sensitive, do not soak too long and moisturize afterward.
c-292.principle: Alkali (pH above about 8.5) saponifies skin oils (triglycerides) into soap and glycerol: $\text{fat} + 3\,\mathrm{OH^-}\to 3\,\text{fatty acid salt (soap)}+\text{glycerol}$. That soap emulsifies on the surface and feels slick.
c-292.example: Soaking 20 minutes at about 40°C in an alkaline spring of pH 9-10 loosens dead skin and sebum, leaving it smooth. At pH 10, $[\mathrm{OH^-}]$ is 1,000 times higher than at neutral pH 7.
c-292.actionItem: If you visit a hot spring or take a bath today, keep alkaline springs to about 10-20 minutes at a time, then pat dry and apply moisturizer right away.

c-293.title: 'Extra Virgin' on Olive Oil Means Acidity of 0.8% or Less
c-293.summary: Extra virgin is a grade for pressed olive oil with free fatty acidity of 0.8% or less that also passes sensory tests. Lower acidity does not always mean better taste, so also check harvest and bottling dates.
c-293.principle: Acidity is the share of free fatty acids (as oleic acid) in oil: $\text{acidity (\%)}=\frac{m_{\mathrm{free\ FA}}}{m_{\mathrm{oil}}}\times100$. Fresher olives have less triglyceride breakdown and so lower acidity, and polyphenols slow oxidation.
c-293.example: Oil at 0.8% or lower is extra virgin, and 2% or lower is virgin. In a 1 L bottle, extra virgin holds about 8 g or less of free fatty acids. Oil is sensitive to light and heat, so dark bottles are better.
c-293.actionItem: When buying olive oil today, check the 'extra virgin' label plus the harvest year and bottling date, choose a dark bottle over a clear one, and store it somewhere cool.

c-294.title: Cover the Terminals of 9V Batteries With Tape Before Storing
c-294.summary: On a 9V battery both terminals sit close together on the same face, so touching metal can short them and cause heating. Cover the terminals with tape or keep each in its own packaging when putting it in a drawer.
c-294.principle: When the terminals touch metal like keys or coins and short, resistance is tiny, a large current $I=\frac{V}{R}$ flows, and Joule heat $P=I^2R$ is produced. For example with $R=0.5\,\Omega$, $I=18\,\mathrm{A}$.
c-294.example: A 9 V battery with about 1.5 Ω internal resistance shorted could in theory reach $I\approx6\,\mathrm{A}$ and about 54 W of heat, getting hot within minutes. Alkaline cells are usually lower than that, but burn and fire risks remain.
c-294.actionItem: Today, cover the terminals of spare 9V batteries in your drawer with clear tape or put them back in the original packaging or a plastic case. Do not store them loose with coins or keys.

c-295.title: Keep Tofu Longer by Submerging It in Water and Changing It Daily
c-295.summary: Opened tofu submerged in clean water in the fridge, with the water changed daily, stays fresh 2-3 days longer. If it smells sour or turns slimy, throw it out.
c-295.principle: Tofu is a soy-protein gel with about 85% water, so bacteria grow easily. Submerging reduces surface contact with air and changes surface water activity $a_w=\frac{p}{p_0}$, and changing the water rinses away grown bacteria and byproducts.
c-295.example: At 4°C, opened tofu soaked in water and changed daily often lasts 3-5 days, while left dry it tends to turn slimy in 1-2 days. Saving one block (300 g, about 2,000 KRW, roughly USD 1.50) from the bin is a real saving.
c-295.actionItem: Today, put leftover tofu in a sealed container with enough clean water (bottled or boiled and cooled) to cover it, refrigerate, and change the water once a day starting tomorrow.

c-296.title: Wash Down Jackets With Neutral Detergent and Dry Them Completely
c-296.summary: Strong alkaline detergent strips the natural oils from down feathers and reduces their loft. Washing with neutral detergent and drying all the way through prevents odor and mold.
c-296.principle: Feather oils (lipids) are saponified and washed away under alkaline conditions: $\text{oil}+3\,\mathrm{OH^-}\to\text{soap}+\text{glycerol}$. Without the oils, feathers clump and the insulating air layer gets thinner.
c-296.example: A typical laundry powder solution is pH about 10-11 and alkaline, while neutral detergent is about pH 7-8. If even 100 g of moisture remains in a 500 g, 800-fill-power jacket, a musty smell and mold can develop after drying.
c-296.actionItem: If you wash a jacket today, use a neutral (wool or down) detergent, rinse well, then dry fully in a low-heat dryer with 2-3 tennis balls or in the shade for several days until dry through.

c-297.title: Take Calcium and Iron Supplements at Different Times
c-297.summary: Calcium and iron supplements can interfere with each other's absorption when taken together. If you take both, space them at least 2 hours apart.
c-297.principle: Divalent cations such as $\mathrm{Ca^{2+}}$ and $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$ compete for the same absorption transporters (such as DMT1) in the small intestine. A high level of one lowers absorption of the other, and calcium above about 500 mg can noticeably reduce iron uptake.
c-297.example: Taking 600 mg of calcium together with 18 mg of iron has been reported to cut iron absorption by about 40-50%. A common routine is iron on an empty stomach with vitamin C and calcium with a meal.
c-297.actionItem: If you take both today, split them: iron in the morning or on an empty stomach and calcium with dinner. If you take prescription medicines, check with a pharmacist first.

c-298.title: Lighters Have Rules for Carrying Onto Planes
c-298.summary: Lighter rules differ by country and airline, but generally only one per person is allowed on your body and it often cannot go in checked luggage. Torch (turbo) types are mostly banned. Check before you go.
c-298.principle: Lighter fuel butane ($\mathrm{C_4H_{10}}$) is a pressurized liquid and highly flammable, burning as $2\,\mathrm{C_4H_{10}}+13\,\mathrm{O_2}\to8\,\mathrm{CO_2}+10\,\mathrm{H_2O}$. When cabin pressure drops, the pressure difference $\Delta P$ across the container grows.
c-298.example: Butane has a vapor pressure of about 2 atm at 20°C. In a cabin (about 0.8 atm) the difference from outside is larger than on the ground, so some lighters may leak fuel or give a bigger flame. A typical disposable lighter holds a few grams of butane.
c-298.actionItem: If you are traveling today, check the lighter rules of your airline and destination country, and leave the lighter at home if you do not need it. If you carry one, keep a single lighter in a pocket so you can show it at security.

c-299.title: Brewed and Acid-Hydrolyzed Soy Sauce Are Made by Different Reactions
c-299.summary: Brewed soy sauce is fermented and aged with microbes from soybeans and wheat, while acid-hydrolyzed sauce breaks soy protein quickly with hydrochloric acid. The label wording and ingredients tell them apart.
c-299.principle: Both hydrolyze protein into amino acids but with different catalysts. Fermentation is $\text{protein}\xrightarrow{\text{enzymes},\ \text{months}}\text{amino acids}$, and acid hydrolysis is $\text{protein}\xrightarrow{\mathrm{HCl},\ \Delta}\text{amino acids}$, done in hours to days.
c-299.example: Brewed soy sauce usually ages 6 months to several years, while acid-hydrolyzed sauce can be made in days, so it is cheaper but has a flatter aroma. Blended sauces on the market mix both, with the ratio on the label.
c-299.actionItem: When buying soy sauce today, check the ingredients for whether it is 100% brewed or a blend with acid-hydrolyzed sauce, and match it to use: brewed for soups and braises, blended for stir-fries and stews.

c-300.title: In Extreme Cold, Diesel's Paraffin Wax Solidifies and the Engine Won't Start
c-300.summary: Paraffin wax in diesel crystallizes in freezing temperatures and clogs the fuel filter so the engine will not start. When a cold snap is forecast, use winter-grade diesel and keep the tank well filled.
c-300.principle: Diesel's n-paraffins (for example $\mathrm{C_{20}H_{42}}$) precipitate as crystals below the cloud point $T_{\mathrm{cp}}$. When $T<T_{\mathrm{cp}}$, wax crystals grow, and at the lower cold filter plugging point the filter blocks.
c-300.example: Summer-grade diesel has a cloud point around 0°C, while winter grade is adjusted down to about -15 to -20°C. On a -10°C morning, leftover summer-grade diesel raises the risk of a failed start.
c-300.actionItem: If a cold wave is forecast today, check that your car has winter-grade diesel and keep the tank more than half full. If it will not start, do not keep cranking, and call a garage or roadside assistance.

c-301.title: A Few Grains of Rice in the Salt Shaker Keep It From Clumping
c-301.summary: When salt clumps from moisture, a few grains of rice help because the rice absorbs moisture first so salt cakes less. It is not perfect, so airtight storage comes first.
c-301.principle: Sodium chloride is deliquescent above about 75% relative humidity, absorbing moisture from the air and dissolving. This critical humidity is $\mathrm{RH}_{\mathrm{c}}\approx75\%$, and above it the grains stick together into lumps.
c-301.example: In humid weather above 80% humidity, an open salt shaker can cake within a day or two. Adding about 10-20 rice grains absorbs some moisture per 100 g of salt and slows clumping.
c-301.actionItem: Today, put 10-20 grains of rice in your salt shaker, close the lid tightly, and keep it somewhere cool and dry rather than beside the stove.

c-302.title: Do Not Use Enzyme Detergent on Wool and Silk
c-302.summary: Wool and silk are protein fibers, so detergent containing protein-digesting enzymes damages them. Use a neutral wool and silk detergent.
c-302.principle: Protease in enzyme detergent hydrolyzes the peptide bonds of proteins: $\mathrm{R{-}CO{-}NH{-}R'}+\mathrm{H_2O}\to\mathrm{R{-}COOH}+\mathrm{H_2N{-}R'}$. Wool keratin and silk fibroin are proteins too, so the same reaction weakens them.
c-302.example: Protease enzymes work best at 30-50°C, which covers typical wash temperatures. Soaking a wool sweater in enzyme detergent at 30°C for just one hour can thin the fibers, dull the sheen or even make holes.
c-302.actionItem: Today, check the care label on your wool or silk clothes, and if a detergent lists 'enzyme (protease)', skip it and gently hand wash in cold water with a neutral wool and silk detergent.

c-303.title: Follow the Storage Temperature on Probiotic Products
c-303.summary: Probiotics are live bacteria that are sensitive to heat and moisture, so follow the storage instructions. If it says refrigerate, do not leave it in a car or a summer delivery box.
c-303.principle: Live bacteria die faster as temperature rises, following $N(t)=N_0\,e^{-kt}$ with $k$ larger at higher temperatures. Spore-forming strains (such as Bacillus) and coated or freeze-dried products are relatively stable at room temperature.
c-303.example: A refrigerate-labeled product kept at 25-30°C can lose a noticeable share of live cells within weeks, and faster above 40°C inside a car. Guaranteed counts usually refer to live cells at the expiry date rather than at manufacture.
c-303.actionItem: Today, check the label of any probiotic you have for 'refrigerate' or 'room temperature', keep refrigerated ones in the fridge, and do not leave them in a summer car or on a windowsill. If you have a health condition, talk to your doctor.

c-304.title: Ask for Medicine by Its Generic Name at Pharmacies Abroad
c-304.summary: The same medicine has different brand names in each country, so at an overseas pharmacy the generic (English) ingredient name is the most accurate. For example, acetaminophen is also called paracetamol abroad.
c-304.principle: Drug generic names (INN) are standardized internationally while brand names vary by maker. The same compound $\mathrm{C_8H_9NO_2}$ is called acetaminophen (US, Korea) or paracetamol (Europe, much of Asia).
c-304.example: A 500 mg acetaminophen product is sold as Tylenol, Panadol, Paracetamol and others depending on the country, but the ingredient is the same. An adult's usual daily maximum is kept at or below 4 g (eight 500 mg tablets).
c-304.actionItem: Today, as part of trip prep, note down or save in your phone the English generic names of medicines you take. At the pharmacy, mention symptoms, current medicines and allergies, and carry a doctor's letter for prescription drugs.

c-305.title: The Difference Between Black, Green and Oolong Tea Is Leaf Oxidation
c-305.summary: Black, oolong and green tea come from the same tea plant but differ in oxidation (fermentation), changing taste and color. Green tea prevents oxidation, while black tea is fully oxidized.
c-305.principle: Polyphenol oxidase (PPO) in tea leaves reacts catechins with oxygen into theaflavins and others: $\text{catechin}+\mathrm{O_2}\xrightarrow{\mathrm{PPO}}\text{theaflavin}$. Green tea is heated first to deactivate the enzyme and stop oxidation.
c-305.example: Green tea has about 0% oxidation, oolong about 10-80%, and black tea nearly 100%. Green tea is usually brewed with about 70-80°C water for 1-2 minutes and black tea with about 90-95°C water for 3-5 minutes.
c-305.actionItem: When buying tea today, check the pack for unoxidized (green), partly oxidized (oolong) or fully oxidized (black), and brew with the matching water temperature and time.

c-306.title: Keep Your Fuel Tank More Than Half Full in Winter
c-306.summary: In winter, an empty fuel tank lets water vapor in the air condense into the fuel, and it can freeze in the lines below zero. Keeping the tank more than half full reduces this.
c-306.principle: Water vapor in the empty space condenses on the cold tank wall. Condensation occurs when temperature falls below the dew point $T_d$, and the more air in the tank, the more vapor can condense. Water freezes at $0^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ or below and blocks fuel flow.
c-306.example: An empty 50 L tank holds about 50 L of humid air, so at 80% relative humidity and 10°C, a few grams of water can condense in theory. A full tank has less air and so less water, cutting the chance that fuel lines freeze on a -10°C morning and block starting.
c-306.actionItem: Today, check the fuel level of your car or heating tank and top up if it is under half. Keeping it above half is an easier winter habit than waiting to fill up completely.

c-307.title: If Coffee Tastes Bitter, Shorten Extraction Instead of Adding More Beans
c-307.summary: If coffee tastes bitter, coarsen the grind or shorten extraction instead of adding more beans. Over-extraction causes bitterness, so you can fix taste without wasting beans.
c-307.principle: Extraction yield is $\text{yield (\%)}=\frac{m_{\mathrm{dissolved\ solids}}}{m_{\mathrm{coffee}}}\times100$, with 18-22% typically ideal. Beyond that, bitter compounds such as chlorogenic acid lactones and phenylindanes are extracted heavily.
c-307.example: With 20 g of coffee, going past 22% yield dissolves more than 4.4 g and tastes bitter and harsh. Targeting 20% from the same 20 g dissolves about 4 g, tasting sweet and balanced. At about 1,000 KRW (roughly USD 0.70) per 20 g of beans, cutting waste adds up.
c-307.actionItem: If your coffee is bitter today, do not add more beans. Grind one step coarser or cut brew time by 20-30 seconds, and keep water at 90-94°C.

c-308.title: Yeast Dies in Water Hotter Than About 55°C
c-308.summary: Yeast for bread dough dies in water that is too hot, so the dough will not rise. Keep water lukewarm to the touch, around 30-38°C.
c-308.principle: Yeast (Saccharomyces) dies quickly above about 55°C where its proteins denature. Activity peaks around 28-35°C, and fermentation $\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6}\to2\,\mathrm{C_2H_5OH}+2\,\mathrm{CO_2}$ makes carbon dioxide that lifts the dough.
c-308.example: With 7 g of yeast in 500 g of flour, 35°C water lets the dough roughly double within an hour, but 60°C water kills most of the yeast and the dough barely rises. It also saves a packet of yeast (about 500 KRW, roughly USD 0.35).
c-308.actionItem: If you bake bread today, check the water temperature with a thermometer or your inner wrist so it is lukewarm at 30-38°C, not hot, and mix salt and yeast apart so they do not touch directly.

c-309.title: Stacking Cold Medicines Can Double Up on Acetaminophen
c-309.summary: Taking a combination cold medicine, a pain reliever and Tylenol separately can duplicate acetaminophen and exceed the daily maximum. Add up the acetaminophen (paracetamol) content across the labels.
c-309.principle: Acetaminophen is mostly metabolized in the liver, but at an overdose the toxic metabolite NAPQI builds up, depleting glutathione and damaging liver cells. Add up the daily total $D_{\mathrm{total}}=\sum D_i$ and keep it at or below 4 g for adults (often advised at 3 g or less).
c-309.example: Four 500 mg Tylenol tablets (2 g) plus three sachets of a combination cold medicine with 325 mg each (about 1 g) already reach 3 g a day. You must tally so that one more Tylenol dose does not push you over 4 g.
c-309.actionItem: If you are taking cold medicine today, check every product label for acetaminophen content, write down the daily total, and stay within the limit. If unsure, ask a pharmacist.

c-310.title: Solid Shampoo and Conditioner Bars Avoid the Liquid Limit When Traveling
c-310.summary: Solid shampoo and conditioner bars are not liquids or gels, so they escape the 100 mL cabin limit and lighten your travel bag. Many airlines and countries do not treat solid soaps as liquids.
c-310.principle: They are made by solidifying surfactants (such as sodium cocoyl isethionate) without water, so they contain almost none. The liquid rule limits volume to $V\le100\,\mathrm{mL}$, so solids are not covered, though the final call rests with the security officer.
c-310.example: A 250 mL liquid shampoo cannot go in the cabin because of its container size, while one shampoo bar (about 50 g) typically lasts about 50-80 washes and weighs about a fifth of a liquid bottle. This fits a long trip.
c-310.actionItem: If you travel today, pack solid shampoo and conditioner bars in a draining tin, and dry them completely before packing rather than putting them in wet. Rules differ by airline and country, so check before departure.

c-311.title: Check Fat Makeup and Trans Fat Labeling on Butter and Margarine
c-311.summary: Butter and margarine differ in fat type, so compare saturated and trans fat on the nutrition label. Margarine is not automatically better or worse, as it varies by product.
c-311.principle: Adding hydrogen to the unsaturated fatty acids of vegetable oil firms it up, and some double bonds turn into trans isomers: $\mathrm{C{=}C}+\mathrm{H_2}\xrightarrow{\mathrm{Ni}}\mathrm{C{-}C}$. This partial hydrogenation can create trans fat.
c-311.example: Butter is about 80% fat, mostly saturated (about 50%), with a small amount of natural trans fat. Older margarines made with partially hydrogenated oil were high in trans fat, but most current products are under 0.5 g per serving and often lower in saturated fat.
c-311.actionItem: When buying butter or margarine today, compare saturated and trans fat per serving on the nutrition label and check whether the ingredients list 'partially hydrogenated oil'.

c-312.title: Read What Fuel Additive Ingredients Do Before Believing the Ads
c-312.summary: For fuel additives, look at which ingredient does what rather than at the advertising claims. Detergent-dispersants clean deposits but do not guarantee a big fuel economy gain.
c-312.principle: Detergent-dispersant surfactant molecules, which have two kinds of ends, surround deposits (carbon) and disperse them in the fuel. Fuel economy is measured as $\eta=\frac{\text{distance}}{\text{fuel}}$, and in a clean engine the gain is very small.
c-312.example: Many products call for a few mL per liter, yet fuel economy gains average about 1-2% and are often limited. For a car at 12 km/L, 2% gives 12.24 km/L, and a 5,000 KRW (roughly USD 3.50) bottle of additive may not be recovered in fuel savings.
c-312.actionItem: If you plan to buy a fuel additive today, check the ingredient description (detergent-dispersant, cetane improver and so on) and the fuel and vehicle types, and see whether advertised economy gains come with conditions.

c-313.title: Feed Leather Shoes With Cream Rather Than Just Polishing Them
c-313.summary: Leather shoes need cream to replenish oils, not just a shine, to stop them drying and cracking. They last longer, saving the cost of new shoes.
c-313.principle: Lipids fill the spaces between collagen fibers and keep leather supple. When these lipids evaporate or wash out, fibers rub together and the leather dries and cracks. Cream refills those gaps with oils and waxes.
c-313.example: If a pair of leather shoes costs about 150,000 KRW (roughly USD 105), caring for them with cream once a month can stretch their life from 2-3 years to 5 or more. Per year, that roughly halves the cost of the shoes. One tin of shoe cream (about 5,000 KRW, roughly USD 3.50) covers dozens of pairs.
c-313.actionItem: Today, wipe the dust off your leather shoes with a dry cloth, apply a thin layer of shoe cream, and after 5 minutes buff with a soft brush or cloth.

c-314.title: Green Vegetables Turn Yellowish When You Add Vinegar
c-314.summary: When blanching green vegetables like spinach or broccoli, adding acid such as vinegar or lemon juice turns the bright green into dull olive. Add acid at the end or just before eating.
c-314.principle: $\mathrm{H^+}$ from the acid replaces the central $\mathrm{Mg^{2+}}$ of chlorophyll, forming pheophytin: $\text{chlorophyll}+2\,\mathrm{H^+}\to\text{pheophytin}+\mathrm{Mg^{2+}}$. Pheophytin is yellow-brown, so the color dulls.
c-314.example: Boiling 100 g of spinach in water with a tablespoon (15 mL) of vinegar lowers the pH from about 7 to around 4, and color starts shifting within 5 minutes. By contrast, blanching briefly in boiling water with a little salt keeps the green longer.
c-314.actionItem: If you blanch greens today, blanch uncovered in boiling water for just 1-2 minutes, rinse in cold water, and sprinkle vinegar or lemon juice just before eating.

c-315.title: Use Retinol at Night and Wear Sunscreen in the Daytime
c-315.summary: Retinol breaks down in light and can make skin more sensitive to the sun, so use it at night and always wear sunscreen by day. If you are pregnant or have a skin condition, talk to a professional first.
c-315.principle: Retinol degrades under UV: $\text{retinol}\xrightarrow{h\nu}\text{degradation products}$. Also, the stratum corneum thins and new skin comes up, so the same UV dose can cause redness more easily.
c-315.example: It is common to start at a low retinol strength (0.1-0.3%) two or three times a week and use SPF 30 or higher sunscreen by day at about 2 mg/cm². SPF 30 blocks about 97% of UVB.
c-315.actionItem: Tonight, use retinol after washing your face, and tomorrow morning put on SPF 30 or higher sunscreen. If stinging or redness is strong, cut back and consult a doctor.

c-316.title: Why Retort Instant Rice Keeps at Room Temperature
c-316.summary: Instant rice lasts at room temperature because it is sealed and then sterilized at high heat and pressure, killing nearly all microbes. It can be stored unrefrigerated until opened, making it good emergency travel food.
c-316.principle: Retort sterilization applies pressure at about 120°C to kill even heat-resistant bacterial spores. The sterilization time is calculated from $F=D_T\,\log\frac{N_0}{N}$, and the oxygen-free seal stops aerobic bacteria from growing.
c-316.example: One pack of instant rice (210 g) is sterilized at about 120°C for roughly 20-30 minutes and typically keeps 6-12 months at room temperature. It can sit unrefrigerated before opening, but after opening it should be eaten right away or refrigerated.
c-316.actionItem: When packing travel bags today, include instant rice as emergency food, and throw away any pack with a bulging lid or a leak. Heat in the microwave as directed on the container.

c-317.title: Sugar Substitutes Like Allulose and Erythritol Each Differ in Sweetness and Properties
c-317.summary: Substitutes such as allulose, erythritol and xylitol differ in sweetness, calories and digestive effects, so choose by use. Too much can cause stomach upset, so start small.
c-317.principle: Sugar alcohols and rare sugars differ in molecular structure, so absorption and calories differ. Erythritol ($\mathrm{C_4H_{10}O_4}$), for example, is mostly absorbed and excreted in urine, giving near-zero calories, and it absorbs heat on dissolving ($\Delta H_{\mathrm{sol}}>0$), creating a cooling feel.
c-317.example: Sugar has about 4 kcal per gram, while erythritol has about 0-0.2 kcal/g and allulose about 0.4 kcal/g. With sugar as 1, sweetness is about 0.7 for both erythritol and allulose. Quantities must be adjusted when replacing sugar.
c-317.actionItem: When buying a sugar substitute today, check the type (allulose, erythritol and so on) and the calories per serving on the label, and start with around 10 g a day to see how your body reacts.

c-318.title: Black Water in Heating Pipes Is Sludge From Oxidized Iron
c-318.summary: If water drained from heating pipes is black, it may be sludge (magnetite) from oxidized iron, and as it builds up, heat transfer worsens. Consider a boiler technician's flush and a corrosion inhibitor check.
c-318.principle: In hot water with almost no oxygen, iron slowly oxidizes: $3\,\mathrm{Fe}+4\,\mathrm{H_2O}\to\mathrm{Fe_3O_4}+4\,\mathrm{H_2}$. The magnetite ($\mathrm{Fe_3O_4}$) that forms is a black powder that builds up and raises thermal resistance.
c-318.example: A 1 mm layer of sludge in pipes and radiators can cut heat transfer by a few percent, making the boiler run longer and raising fuel cost by about 5-10%. A flush usually costs several hundred thousand KRW (a few hundred USD), but savings and longer equipment life can repay it.
c-318.actionItem: Today, check when your heating pipes were last flushed, and if it has been several years, ask a boiler technician for an inspection. Do not dismantle the pipes or touch drained water yourself.

c-319.title: Freezer Burn Is Where Moisture Left an Air-Exposed Surface
c-319.summary: The white, dry patches on meat or vegetables kept long in the freezer are freezer burn. It is not harmful to eat but is tough and loses flavor, and squeezing out air and sealing prevents it.
c-319.principle: In the freezer, surface ice sublimates straight to vapor without going through liquid, so moisture leaves: $\mathrm{H_2O(s)}\to\mathrm{H_2O(g)}$. The dried surface meets air, so fats oxidize and give off-flavors.
c-319.example: Unwrapped meat in a -18°C freezer loses a few percent of surface moisture within weeks and dries white. Pressing air out with vacuum or zip bags keeps quality for 3-6 months or more and reduces thrown-away food (a few thousand KRW a month or more).
c-319.actionItem: Today, pack meat and vegetables for the freezer in single portions in zip bags, squeeze out as much air as you can, seal and write the date. For parts that already have freezer burn, trim them off or use them in soups and stews.

c-320.title: Dissolve Curry and Sauce Powder in Cold Water First to Avoid Lumps
c-320.summary: Adding curry or sauce powder straight into hot liquid cooks only the outside and forms lumps. Dissolve it first in cold or lukewarm water, or turn off the heat and mix it in a little at a time.
c-320.principle: When starch granules meet hot water, their surface gelatinizes first into a sticky gel film that keeps water from reaching the powder inside. Gelatinization starts around 60-70°C and happens first at the surface where $T>T_{\mathrm{gel}}$.
c-320.example: Dumping 100 g of curry powder into 90°C broth forms lumps several millimeters across as the surface gelatinizes, but dissolving it first in 200 mL of 20-30°C water spreads the particles evenly with almost no lumps.
c-320.actionItem: If you make curry or sauce today, dissolve the powder in cold water first and strain it, or turn off the heat and add it a little at a time while stirring, then bring it back to a gentle simmer.

c-321.title: AHA and BHA exfoliants depend on pH and concentration
c-321.summary: What decides both results and irritation is the product's pH and acid concentration, not just the ingredient name. Even a mild acid can sting if the pH is low.
c-321.principle: Acids ionize according to $\mathrm{pH} = \mathrm{p}K_a + \log\frac{[\mathrm{A^-}]}{[\mathrm{HA}]}$, and only the un-ionized free acid ($\mathrm{HA}$) acts on skin. The lower the pH is below $\mathrm{p}K_a$, the larger the free-acid share.
c-321.example: A 10% glycolic acid product ($\mathrm{p}K_a$ about 3.83) is 50% free acid at pH 3.83 but about 87% at pH 3.0, so it irritates more. Salicylic acid ($\mathrm{p}K_a$ about 2.97) is typically formulated near pH 3-4.
c-321.actionItem: If you use an exfoliant today, check its acid type, concentration and pH, start with 2 times a week or fewer, and apply sunscreen the next day.

c-322.title: Durian is banned from many hotels because of its smell
c-322.summary: Durian is banned in hotels and on transit not because it is toxic, but because its smell is overwhelming even in tiny amounts.
c-322.principle: Esters ($\mathrm{RCOOH + R'OH \rightleftharpoons RCOOR' + H_2O}$) and sulfur compounds (thiols, $\mathrm{R{-}SH}$) have odor thresholds in the ppb range, so trace amounts are detectable.
c-322.example: 1 ppb is one part per billion by volume, which equals only about 0.03 mL of vapor in a 30 m³ room. That is why the smell lingers in a whole room and in the AC filter.
c-322.actionItem: Before a Southeast Asia trip, check your lodging's durian rule, and eat durian at the shop or outdoors.

c-323.title: Moisturizer ingredients do different jobs: ceramides, glycerin, oils
c-323.summary: A good moisturizer pairs an ingredient that draws in water, one that fills gaps, and one that blocks evaporation.
c-323.principle: Humectants (glycerin) attract water, emollients (ceramides) fill gaps between skin cells, and occlusives (petrolatum) block evaporation. Water movement follows $J = -D\frac{\Delta C}{\Delta x}$.
c-323.example: Glycerin is typically used at 5-10%, and petrolatum is known to cut transepidermal water loss by more than 90%. A product with all three lasts longer in dry winter air than a single-ingredient one.
c-323.actionItem: Today, check the ingredient list for glycerin, ceramides and an oil or petrolatum, and apply within 3 minutes after showering.

c-324.title: Check your fireplace or stove chimney for creosote every year
c-324.summary: Tar from wood smoke condenses on chimney walls, and the buildup can cause a chimney fire, so inspect it every year.
c-324.principle: Tar and soot vapors from incomplete combustion condense on cool chimney walls as creosote. Oxygen-starved burning, $\mathrm{C_xH_y + O_2 \to C + CO + H_2O}$, produces more unburned material.
c-324.example: NFPA 211 in the US advises cleaning when deposits reach about 3 mm (1/8 inch). Wet wood above 20% moisture lowers the burn temperature and speeds up buildup.
c-324.actionItem: Today, check that your firewood is dried to 20% moisture or less, and book a professional chimney inspection and sweep.

c-325.title: Butter absorbs odors when stored next to strong-smelling foods
c-325.summary: Butter is about 80% fat, which dissolves and soaks up odor molecules from foods like kimchi or fish.
c-325.principle: Fat is nonpolar, so it dissolves the nonpolar volatile molecules that carry odors. The partition coefficient is $K = \frac{C_{\mathrm{fat}}}{C_{\mathrm{water}}}$, and $\log K = 3$ means a 1,000 times higher concentration in fat.
c-325.example: A 200 g block of butter holds about 160 g of fat. Left uncovered next to kimchi for a few days, it picks up the smell and may end up thrown away.
c-325.actionItem: Today, put your butter in its wrapper inside a sealed container and keep it away from strong-smelling foods.

c-326.title: Why glasses turn cloudy in the dishwasher
c-326.summary: Cloudiness can be a mineral film or actual etching of the glass surface. A vinegar soak tells you which.
c-326.principle: Soft water and alkaline detergent at high temperature dissolve the silicate network of glass and etch the surface. $\mathrm{SiO_2 + 2OH^- \to SiO_3^{2-} + H_2O}$
c-326.example: Etching is permanent, but a hard-water lime film vanishes after 5 minutes in white vinegar. Using less detergent and an eco cycle around 55 °C reduces etching.
c-326.actionItem: Today, soak a cloudy glass in white vinegar for 5 minutes to see if it is film, and use only the recommended detergent dose.

c-327.title: Replace mascara every 3 to 6 months
c-327.summary: Mascara goes right next to the eyes and gets air pumped in with every use, so bacteria build up; replace it within 3-6 months of opening.
c-327.principle: After opening, the preservative is gradually used up and bacteria grow as $N = N_0\,2^{t/t_d}$. Each time the wand goes in and out it pushes air in, causing drying and contamination.
c-327.example: Under ideal conditions with a 20-minute doubling time, one cell becomes $2^{18}$, about 262,000, in 6 hours. If you have itchy or red eyes, suspect an old mascara first.
c-327.actionItem: Today, write the opening date on your mascara tube, and replace it with a new one if it is older than 3 months.

c-328.title: Rice abroad tastes different because of its amylose content
c-328.summary: Rice abroad can come out fluffy and separate or sticky because the amylose-to-amylopectin ratio differs.
c-328.principle: More amylose (linear) keeps grains separate and firm, while more amylopectin (branched) makes rice sticky. $\text{amylose \%} = \frac{m_{\mathrm{amylose}}}{m_{\mathrm{amylose}}+m_{\mathrm{amylopectin}}}\times 100$
c-328.example: Korean and Japanese short-grain rice has roughly 17-20% amylose, long-grain indica about 22-28%, and glutinous rice nearly 0%. Long-grain rice usually needs 1.5-2 times its volume of water.
c-328.actionItem: Today, check whether your rice package says short, medium or long grain, and cook it with the water ratio printed on the package.

c-329.title: Check mouthwash for alcohol-free formulas and CPC
c-329.summary: Pick a mouthwash by its antibacterial ingredient (CPC) and whether it has alcohol, which can dry out your mouth.
c-329.principle: CPC (cetylpyridinium chloride) is a cationic surfactant that sticks to negatively charged bacterial membranes and disrupts them. The attraction follows $F = k\frac{q_1 q_2}{r^2}$.
c-329.example: CPC products are usually 0.05-0.07%, so one 20 mL rinse contains about 10-14 mg. Some products contain 20% ethanol or more, so people prone to dry mouth may prefer alcohol-free.
c-329.actionItem: Today, check the label for CPC and ethanol, then rinse for 30 seconds and spit it out rather than swallowing.

c-330.title: Window caulk smell is acetic acid released during curing
c-330.summary: The vinegar smell of caulk is acetic acid released as the silicone cures, and it fades once curing is done.
c-330.principle: Acetoxy silicone reacts with moisture in the air, releasing acetic acid as it crosslinks. $\mathrm{R{-}Si(OCOCH_3)_3 + 3H_2O \to R{-}Si(OH)_3 + 3CH_3COOH}$
c-330.example: The surface skins over in about 10-30 minutes, and a 3 mm bead takes about 24 hours to cure fully. Acetic acid can corrode metal and marble, so use neutral-cure silicone there.
c-330.actionItem: If you apply caulk today, keep a window open to ventilate for 24 hours, and choose neutral-cure silicone for metal or stone.

c-331.title: Olive oil turning cloudy and solid in the fridge isn't spoiled
c-331.summary: Olive oil that goes cloudy and solid in the fridge is not spoiled; its fat has crystallized, and it clears again at room temperature.
c-331.principle: Even unsaturated fatty acids crystallize below their melting point. The melting temperature follows $T_m = \frac{\Delta H}{\Delta S}$, and olive oil starts to cloud below about 5-10 °C.
c-331.example: At 4 °C in the fridge it turns cloudy, but 30-60 minutes at 20-25 °C clears it. For oxidation, a dark, cool room-temperature spot is better than the fridge.
c-331.actionItem: Today, let cloudy olive oil sit at room temperature for 30 minutes instead of microwaving it, and store it in a dark cupboard from now on.

c-332.title: Make caramel by melting sugar without stirring
c-332.summary: You avoid stirring when making caramel to stop sugar crystals from re-forming in a chain reaction.
c-332.principle: One stray sugar crystal can seed crystallization of the whole syrup. Above 160 °C, hydrolysis and dehydration cause browning. $\mathrm{C_{12}H_{22}O_{11} + H_2O \to C_6H_{12}O_6 + C_6H_{12}O_6}$
c-332.example: Boiling 200 g sugar with 50 mL water reaches a golden caramel at about 170-180 °C after 5-10 minutes. Caramel at that temperature can cause serious burns if it splatters.
c-332.actionItem: If you make caramel today, swirl the pan instead of stirring and wash crystals off the pot wall with a wet brush.

c-333.title: Red skin under metal jewelry may be nickel allergy
c-333.summary: If skin turns red and itchy under earrings or a watch buckle, nickel in the metal may be the cause. A dermatologist can confirm it.
c-333.principle: Nickel in the metal is oxidized by sweat and dissolves as ions. $\mathrm{Ni \to Ni^{2+} + 2e^-}$ These ions can bind skin proteins and trigger contact dermatitis.
c-333.example: The EU limits nickel release from items in prolonged skin contact to $0.5\ \mu\mathrm{g/cm^2}$ per week. Roughly 1 in 10 people are reported to be nickel-sensitive.
c-333.actionItem: Today, check for a nickel-free label on any jewelry that keeps itching, and see a dermatologist if symptoms continue.

c-334.title: Wasabi's heat only appears when grated and fades fast
c-334.summary: Real wasabi's heat is created when its cells are crushed by grating, and it is volatile, so it fades quickly.
c-334.principle: When cells break, the enzyme myrosinase splits the glycoside sinigrin into pungent allyl isothiocyanate. $\mathrm{C_{10}H_{16}KNO_9S_2 + H_2O \to C_4H_5NS + C_6H_{12}O_6 + KHSO_4}$
c-334.example: The heat is strongest within minutes of grating and drops sharply in 15-30 minutes. Many tube wasabi products are mainly horseradish.
c-334.actionItem: If you use fresh wasabi today, grate it right before eating and keep it covered, and check the ingredients on tube products.

c-335.title: More dish soap foam doesn't mean better cleaning
c-335.summary: Lots of foam and good grease removal are separate things; foam can come from stabilizers.
c-335.principle: Surfactants form micelles above the critical micelle concentration (CMC) and wrap around grease. Surface tension falls until the CMC and stays almost constant after that.
c-335.example: The CMC of SDS is about 8.2 mM, or about 2.4 g per liter. Adding more soap beyond that does not boost cleaning much and only makes rinsing harder.
c-335.actionItem: Today, use only a pea-sized amount of dish soap and judge by whether grease is gone, not by how much foam there is.

c-336.title: Heat-generating thermal underwear warms by adsorbing sweat vapor
c-336.summary: Heat-generating underwear feels warm because water vapor from your body releases heat when it sticks to the fibers; the effect is modest and short-lived.
c-336.principle: When water vapor attaches to fibers, heat is released much like condensation. $Q = m\,L$, and water's condensation heat $L$ is about $2.26\ \mathrm{MJ/kg}$.
c-336.example: Adsorbing 10 g of moisture releases up to about 23 kJ, but it stops once the fibers saturate. If you sweat heavily and the fabric gets wet, it draws heat away and you feel colder.
c-336.actionItem: Today, wear a thin layer over thermal underwear, and remove a layer when you start to sweat so the fabric stays dry.

c-337.title: Remove labels and caps from PET bottles so they can be recycled
c-337.summary: PET bottles become good recycled material only if you remove the label and rinse them, so they do not mix with other plastics.
c-337.principle: Recycling separates sinking PET from floating PP and PE by density, $\rho = \frac{m}{V}$, then melts it. PET melts near 250 °C, PP near 165 °C and PE around 110-130 °C.
c-337.example: PET has a density of about 1.38 g/cm³ while PP and PE are about 0.9 g/cm³, so they separate in water. If a 2 g cap is mixed with a 20 g bottle, contaminants reach about 10%.
c-337.actionItem: Today, empty and rinse your PET bottle, peel off the label, and put it in the clear-PET collection bin.

c-338.title: Meringue won't whip with even a drop of grease
c-338.summary: The most common reason meringue won't rise is a trace of fat on the bowl or in the whites.
c-338.principle: Egg white proteins unfold at the air-water boundary and form a film that holds the bubbles. Fat takes up that spot first and blocks film formation. The pressure difference across a bubble film is $\Delta P = \frac{4\gamma}{r}$.
c-338.example: Three egg whites (about 100 g) are roughly 90% water and 10% protein, while yolk is about 30% fat, so even a drop sharply cuts the volume. Plastic bowls often hold traces of oil.
c-338.actionItem: If you make meringue today, wipe a glass or steel bowl with vinegar or lemon juice and separate each white into a small bowl first.

c-339.title: Do a patch test two days before covering gray hair
c-339.summary: Hair dye allergy can appear suddenly, so patch-test behind the ear or on the inner arm 48 hours before dyeing.
c-339.principle: Oxidative dyes such as para-phenylenediamine (PPD) form reactive intermediates with hydrogen peroxide that bind skin proteins and can cause allergy. $\mathrm{C_6H_4(NH_2)_2 \xrightarrow{H_2O_2} \text{reactive intermediates}}$
c-339.example: The EU limits PPD on the head to 2% after mixing. Apply a small amount no bigger than a coin and watch for 48 hours; if there is redness, itching or swelling, do not dye.
c-339.actionItem: If you plan to dye soon, do the patch test two days ahead with a small amount behind the ear, and skip dyeing if any reaction appears, seeking care if it is severe.

c-340.title: Proof on a foreign liquor bottle is twice the ABV
c-340.summary: On US bottles, proof is twice the alcohol by volume (ABV), so 80 proof means 40%.
c-340.principle: The US system is $\text{proof} = 2 \times \text{ABV}$. The old British proof used a different basis, where 100 proof was about 57.15%, so check by country.
c-340.example: A 45 mL (1.5 oz) pour of 80 proof whiskey holds $45 \times 0.40 = 18\ \mathrm{mL}$ ethanol, about 14.2 g, which is one US standard drink. The same pour at 100 proof (50%) holds about 17.8 g.
c-340.actionItem: Today, divide any foreign bottle's proof by 2 to get the ABV, and keep track of how much you drink.

c-341.title: Water filters: activated carbon and reverse osmosis remove different things
c-341.summary: Activated carbon mostly removes organics such as chlorine and odor, while reverse osmosis mostly removes dissolved ions. Decide what you need to remove before buying.
c-341.principle: Carbon adsorbs onto its surface, while reverse osmosis applies pressure above the osmotic pressure $\pi = iMRT$ so only water passes through the semipermeable membrane.
c-341.example: The osmotic pressure of 500 mg/L NaCl (about 8.6 mmol/L) at 25 °C is about 0.42 atm. Home RO units usually apply 3-4 bar and remove most ions.
c-341.actionItem: Today, check when your water filter is due for replacement, and verify its claims through an official certification mark.

c-342.title: Camping lantern mantles glow because of rare-earth oxides
c-342.summary: A gas lantern's bright light is not the flame but a rare-earth oxide mantle heated by it.
c-342.principle: When the oxide mantle is heated to about 2,000 K, it radiates strongly toward visible wavelengths. The peak wavelength follows $\lambda_{\max} T = 2898\ \mu\mathrm{m\cdot K}$.
c-342.example: At 2,000 K, $\lambda_{\max}$ is about 1.45 μm. Yttrium and cerium mantles emit much more visible light than a bare flame from the same fuel. Older mantles used radioactive thorium oxide.
c-342.actionItem: Today, burn a new mantle off outdoors for its first use, do not touch the ash, and look for a thorium-free label.

c-343.title: Paper cups aren't recycled as ordinary paper because of their polyethylene lining
c-343.summary: Paper cups have a plastic film for waterproofing, so putting them in the regular paper bin makes recycling difficult.
c-343.principle: The polyethylene (PE) inside a paper cup does not dissolve in water and floats at $\rho \approx 0.92\ \mathrm{g/cm^3}$, so it is hard to separate from fiber during pulping.
c-343.example: One paper cup weighs about 10 g and the PE coating is roughly 5% of that. Without a dedicated process, that coating can ruin the quality of a whole paper batch.
c-343.actionItem: Today, bring your own tumbler, and if you do use a paper cup, check your local sorting rule and collect it separately.

c-344.title: Cream whips firm only when it is cold
c-344.summary: Cream whips into stiff peaks only when very cold; lukewarm cream will not rise no matter how long you whisk.
c-344.principle: When cold, fat inside the globules is crystallized, so whipping makes the globules partly clump into a network that traps air bubbles. Melted fat cannot build that network.
c-344.example: Whipping 200 mL of cream with 35% or more fat at 4 °C roughly doubles the volume in 3-5 minutes. Above 20 °C it barely rises, and overwhipping splits it into butter and buttermilk.
c-344.actionItem: Today, chill the cream and bowl for 10+ minutes before whipping, and stop as soon as stiff peaks form.

c-345.title: Don't hold whitening toothpaste peroxide in your mouth for long
c-345.summary: Peroxide in whitening toothpaste or strips can irritate gums, so use it only for the stated time.
c-345.principle: Hydrogen peroxide oxidizes and breaks down stain molecules while releasing oxygen. $2\mathrm{H_2O_2} \to 2\mathrm{H_2O} + \mathrm{O_2}$ That same reactivity can irritate mucous membranes.
c-345.example: The EU limits hydrogen peroxide in ordinary toothpaste to 0.1% and requires dental supervision for 0.1-6% whitening products. Holding it longer than directed increases gum irritation and sensitivity.
c-345.actionItem: Today, use any whitening product only for the time on the label, and stop and consult a dentist if your gums sting.

c-346.title: Don't drink melted snow without treating it
c-346.summary: Snow looks clean but collects airborne pollutants and microbes, so melted snow should be boiled before drinking.
c-346.principle: Snow crystals trap dust and fine particles as they form and fall. Boiling kills microbes but does not remove heavy metals or chemicals. The water yield depends on snow density, $V_{\mathrm{water}} \approx \frac{V_{\mathrm{snow}}}{10}$.
c-346.example: Melting 10 L of fresh snow gives about 1 L of water, and the usual rule is to boil for at least 1 minute (3 minutes above 2,000 m). Avoid snow near roads or that is discolored.
c-346.actionItem: Today, in an emergency, collect only clean fresh snow, start with a little water in the pot, melt and boil it, and otherwise carry bottled water.

c-347.title: Lactose-free milk is milk with the lactose broken down in advance
c-347.summary: Lactose-free milk has its lactose pre-digested, so it suits lactose intolerance, but its milk proteins remain, so it is not suitable for milk allergy.
c-347.principle: The enzyme lactase hydrolyzes lactose into glucose and galactose. $\mathrm{C_{12}H_{22}O_{11} + H_2O \xrightarrow{\text{lactase}} C_6H_{12}O_6 + C_6H_{12}O_6}$
c-347.example: Regular milk has about 4.7-5 g of lactose per 100 mL, so 200 mL holds about 9.5 g. The EU lactose-free standard is 0.01 g per 100 g or less, and the released sugars make it taste slightly sweeter.
c-347.actionItem: Today, if lactose upsets your stomach, choose a lactose-free product, but avoid both regular and lactose-free milk if you have a milk allergy.

c-348.title: Turn on the hood when cooking on a gas stove because it releases nitrogen dioxide
c-348.summary: A gas flame produces nitrogen dioxide that can degrade air in a small kitchen, so run the hood while cooking.
c-348.principle: In a hot flame, nitrogen and oxygen from air react ($\mathrm{N_2 + O_2 \to 2NO}$) and then oxidize further. $2\mathrm{NO} + \mathrm{O_2} \to 2\mathrm{NO_2}$
c-348.example: Measurements in small unventilated kitchens have reported nitrogen dioxide above the WHO 1-hour guideline of $200\ \mu\mathrm{g/m^3}$. A hood that vents outdoors lowers it substantially.
c-348.actionItem: Today, switch the hood on before you start cooking and keep it running about 10 minutes after turning off the flame.

c-349.title: Leftover cooking oil can be turned into laundry soap
c-349.summary: Instead of pouring leftover cooking oil down the drain, you can collect it and react it with lye to make soap.
c-349.principle: Saponification turns triglycerides and NaOH into soap and glycerol. $\mathrm{C_3H_5(OOCR)_3 + 3NaOH \to C_3H_5(OH)_3 + 3RCOONa}$
c-349.example: Soybean oil needs about 0.135 g NaOH per gram of oil, so 500 g of oil needs about 68 g. Lye is strongly caustic, so goggles and gloves are essential, and the soap cures for about 4 weeks.
c-349.actionItem: Today, strain leftover oil through a coffee filter into a sealed bottle, and never pour it down the drain.

c-350.title: One drop of water makes melted chocolate seize up
c-350.summary: A little water in melted chocolate can suddenly turn it from smooth to a stiff, grainy lump.
c-350.principle: Sugar and cocoa particles absorb water and form sticky syrup films that glue the particles together, sharply raising viscosity. This is called seizing.
c-350.example: Just a few grams of water, about 1-2% of 200 g of chocolate, is enough to seize it. Adding much more water, to roughly 20% or beyond, can make it smooth again as a thin ganache.
c-350.actionItem: Today, when melting chocolate, dry the bowl and spatula and keep steam and water from the double boiler out of the bowl.

c-351.title: Wash cutting boards right after use and dry them completely
c-351.summary: Bacteria need moisture to multiply, so washing your cutting board right away and drying it completely is the key.
c-351.principle: Water activity, which shows how available water is, is $a_w = \frac{p}{p_0}$, and many pathogens grow fast at $a_w$ of about 0.9 or higher.
c-351.example: The surface of raw meat has an $a_w$ of about 0.99, which suits bacterial growth. Standing the board up to dry with airflow reduces surface moisture and limits growth.
c-351.actionItem: Today, wash your board with hot water and detergent right after use and stand it up to dry fully, keeping raw-meat and vegetable boards separate.

c-352.title: Boiling Christmas-market Glühwein drives off the aroma
c-352.summary: Mulled wine should be heated only until it steams, not boiled, so more of its aroma and alcohol stays.
c-352.principle: Ethanol boils at about 78 °C, lower than water, so it evaporates first when heated. The vapor pressure of a mixture follows $P = x_{\mathrm{EtOH}}\,P^{\circ}_{\mathrm{EtOH}}$ (Raoult's law).
c-352.example: A 750 mL bottle of 12% wine contains about 90 mL of ethanol. It is usually served at 60-70 °C, and boiling above 78 °C expels alcohol and aroma compounds quickly.
c-352.actionItem: Today, warm mulled wine on low heat below 70 °C and remove the spices before it boils.

c-353.title: The ABC marking on a fire extinguisher shows fire types
c-353.summary: The A, B and C on an extinguisher show which fires it can fight, and an ABC dry-powder unit is the usual home choice.
c-353.principle: In Korean and US labeling, A is ordinary combustibles, B is flammable liquids and C is electrical fires. Monoammonium phosphate decomposes on heating and suppresses the combustion chain reaction. $\mathrm{NH_4H_2PO_4 \to NH_3 + H_3PO_4}$
c-353.example: A 3.3 kg home powder extinguisher usually discharges in about 10-20 seconds, so know how to use it beforehand. In Europe the classes differ, for example C means gas fires, so check local standards.
c-353.actionItem: Today, check that your extinguisher's pressure gauge is in the green range and keep it within easy reach.

c-354.title: Reusable hand warmers use sodium acetate's heat of crystallization
c-354.summary: Reusable hand warmers use the heat released when a supersaturated solution crystallizes all at once, and boiling them in water resets them.
c-354.principle: Sodium acetate trihydrate melts at about 58 °C, and when the supercooled liquid crystallizes it releases heat of fusion. $Q = m\,\Delta H_{\mathrm{fus}}$, with $\Delta H_{\mathrm{fus}}$ about 265 J/g.
c-354.example: A 100 g pack releases about 26 kJ as it crystallizes, and its surface rises to around 50 °C. Leaving the same pack in boiling water for about 10 minutes turns it clear again.
c-354.actionItem: Today, boil a used warmer in water until every crystal dissolves, cool it slowly, and avoid holding it on bare skin for long.

c-355.title: Blocking oxygen keeps opened wine good for about four more days
c-355.summary: Oxygen is the main reason opened wine goes off, so re-corking and refrigerating it usually buys 3-5 more days.
c-355.principle: Oxygen and acetic acid bacteria convert ethanol to acetic acid via acetaldehyde. $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2OH + O_2 \to CH_3COOH + H_2O}$ The rate follows $k = Ae^{-E_a/RT}$, roughly halving for each 10 °C drop.
c-355.example: Re-corked and refrigerated, red and white both usually last 3-5 days, while left open at room temperature they decline in 1-2 days. If little remains, move it to a smaller bottle to cut the air inside.
c-355.actionItem: Today, cork leftover wine and refrigerate it right away, and take red out 20 minutes before drinking.

c-356.title: White crystals at the bottom of a wine bottle are tartrate deposits
c-356.summary: White granules at the bottom of a bottle or on the cork are tartrate crystals, not spoilage, and are harmless.
c-356.principle: Potassium hydrogen tartrate (KHT) becomes less soluble at low temperature and precipitates. $\mathrm{KHC_4H_4O_6(s) \rightleftharpoons K^+ + HC_4H_4O_6^-}$ with $K_{sp} = [\mathrm{K^+}][\mathrm{HC_4H_4O_6^-}]$.
c-356.example: Wine usually contains 1.5-4 g/L tartaric acid, and crystals form slowly in cold storage such as a fridge. The same substance is the cream of tartar used in baking.
c-356.actionItem: Today, if you see crystals, do not throw the wine out; stand the bottle upright and pour slowly, leaving the sediment behind.

c-357.title: Don't put aroma oil or detergent into a humidifier
c-357.summary: Only clean water belongs in a humidifier tank. Oils or detergents turn into fine particles that you then breathe in.
c-357.principle: An ultrasonic humidifier atomizes water into fine droplets, carrying dissolved substances into the air with it. The mass of non-volatile material released is $m = C \times V_{\mathrm{mist}}$.
c-357.example: At a mist output of about 300 mL per hour, a 1% additive means roughly 3 mL of oil or detergent aerosolized every hour. Tap-water minerals (assuming 150 mg/L) also become about 45 mg of white dust per hour.
c-357.actionItem: Today, change the humidifier water daily, use a dedicated diffuser for aromas, and wash the tank weekly.

c-358.title: E10 at foreign pumps is gasoline blended with ethanol
c-358.summary: E10 is gasoline with about 10% ethanol; most gasoline cars can use it, but it has slightly less energy.
c-358.principle: Ethanol has about 21 MJ/L of energy by volume, lower than gasoline's roughly 32 MJ/L. $E_{\mathrm{E10}} = 0.9E_{\mathrm{gas}} + 0.1E_{\mathrm{EtOH}}$, and octane rises slightly.
c-358.example: E10 delivers about 30.9 MJ/L, around 3% less than gasoline, so a car that does 14 km/L would do about 13.6 km/L. Check the fuel-cap label to confirm your car suits E10.
c-358.actionItem: Today, when you pick up a rental car, check the fuel-cap label (gasoline, diesel, E10-compatible) and do not mix up diesel and gasoline.

c-359.title: Smoke detectors differ: photoelectric versus ionization
c-359.summary: Different smoke detector types respond best to different fires, with photoelectric stronger on slow smoldering fires.
c-359.principle: An ionization alarm uses americium-241 to ionize air and sounds when smoke particles reduce the current, while a photoelectric alarm senses light scattered by smoke particles.
c-359.example: Ionization responds faster to small particles (about 0.01-0.3 μm) from flaming fires, and photoelectric to larger particles (about 0.3-10 μm) from smoldering fires. An ionization unit holds about 30-40 kBq of americium.
c-359.actionItem: Today, press the test button on your detector, and replace it if the manufacture date on the back is over 10 years old.

c-360.title: Only short trips in a diesel car clog the particulate filter
c-360.summary: If you only drive a diesel car on short trips, exhaust never gets hot enough and soot builds up in the diesel particulate filter (DPF).
c-360.principle: Soot in a DPF has to be burned off in regeneration. $\mathrm{C + O_2 \to CO_2}$ happens at about 350-450 °C with a catalyst, and active regeneration at about 600 °C.
c-360.example: On short trips the exhaust stays below 200 °C and regeneration never happens. That is why you occasionally need a drive of 20-30 minutes or more at highway speed to burn the filter clean.
c-360.actionItem: This week, drive 20-30 minutes or more at a steady highway speed, and have it checked at a garage if a warning light is on.

c-361.title: A little baking soda tenderizes tough meat
c-361.summary: A very small amount of baking soda raises the pH of tough meat so it holds more water and turns tender.
c-361.principle: Muscle proteins hold water worst near their isoelectric point (pH about 5-5.5). Raising meat pH (about 5.5-5.7) with baking soda adds negative charge so proteins repel each other and hold more water. $\mathrm{NaHCO_3 \rightleftharpoons Na^+ + HCO_3^-}$
c-361.example: Toss 450 g of sliced meat with about 2.5 g (0.5%) of baking soda for 15 minutes, then rinse. Too much gives a soapy taste and mushy texture.
c-361.actionItem: Today, if stir-fry meat is tough, coat it with 0.5% or less baking soda for only 15 minutes, rinse well, and then cook.

c-362.title: Milk sometimes curdles in hot coffee
c-362.summary: Milk curdling in coffee is proteins clumping because of acidity and heat, and fresh milk is usually harmless.
c-362.principle: The isoelectric point of milk casein is about pH 4.6, so as pH approaches it the charge drops and the proteins clump together. Heat speeds up this aggregation.
c-362.example: Milk is about pH 6.7 and coffee about 4.8-5.1. Older milk already has a lower pH and curdles more easily, so if it smells sour, discard it rather than drink it.
c-362.actionItem: Today, pour milk into the cup first or use warmed milk for your coffee, and throw it out if it smells sour.

c-363.title: Inhaling helium from balloon gas is dangerous
c-363.summary: Inhaling helium changes your voice, but it displaces oxygen and can cause suffocation, so it is dangerous.
c-363.principle: The oxygen partial pressure in breathing gas is $P_{\mathrm{O_2}} = F_{\mathrm{O_2}} \times P$. Pure helium has $F_{\mathrm{O_2}} = 0$, so it pushes oxygen out of the lungs. Sound speed, $v = \sqrt{\frac{\gamma RT}{M}}$, is much higher in helium, which raises the voice.
c-363.example: Air is 20.9% oxygen while 100% helium has 0%. Sound speed in helium is about 1,007 m/s, roughly 3 times that in air (about 343 m/s), and breathing directly from a pressurized tank can injure the lungs.
c-363.actionItem: Today, when inflating balloons, do not inhale the helium, and ventilate in a closed room.

c-364.title: Don't send high-speed film through airport X-rays
c-364.summary: Airport X-rays can fog film, so for high-speed film it is safer to ask for a hand inspection.
c-364.principle: When silver halide crystals absorb light or X-ray photons, they form a latent image of silver atoms. $\mathrm{AgBr + h\nu \to Ag + Br}$ Exposure accumulates.
c-364.example: Film rated ISO 800 or higher can fog after several scans, and X-rays for checked baggage are stronger. Because exposure adds up, keep the number of scans on a trip low.
c-364.actionItem: Today, put your film in a clear bag, ask for a hand inspection at security, and do not pack it in checked luggage.

c-365.title: Judge perfume lasting power and price by EDP or EDT strength
c-365.summary: With perfume, the fragrance concentration (%) tells you more about lasting power and price than the name does.
c-365.principle: The higher the fragrance concentration, the slower the evaporation and the longer it lasts. Eau de parfum (EDP) is about 15-20%, eau de toilette (EDT) about 5-15% and eau de cologne (EDC) about 2-4%.
c-365.example: In a 50 mL bottle, 15% EDP holds about 7.5 mL of fragrance oil and 8% EDT about 4 mL, so EDP usually costs more. EDT typically lasts about 3-4 hours and EDP about 5-8 hours.
c-365.actionItem: Before buying perfume, spray it on your inner forearm and check how it smells after 4 hours.

c-366.title: The aerogel in insoles and gloves is mostly air held in silica
c-366.summary: Aerogel in cold-weather gear is a silica structure that is mostly air, so even a thin layer blocks heat well.
c-366.principle: Nano-sized pores smaller than the mean free path of air molecules (about 68 nm) block heat transfer. $\lambda = \frac{k_B T}{\sqrt{2}\,\pi d^2 P}$ and heat flow is $Q = \frac{kA\,\Delta T}{L}$.
c-366.example: Silica aerogel has a thermal conductivity of about 0.015-0.02 W/m·K, lower than still air (about 0.026). For an area of 0.02 m², a thickness of 3 mm and a 20 K difference with $k = 0.02$, heat loss is about 2.7 W.
c-366.actionItem: Today, check the actual aerogel content and thickness of your insoles and gloves, and keep them dry because wetness reduces insulation.
